[b]VESPERTINE EVENING[/b]

March 15th, 2026.

The Empire had only just begun to steady itself from the political fracture of separation, the unexpected end of union that had once been trumpeted as immortal. The news had only reached the public hours before. The Empire of Vespurias remained, but the embarrassment of Elseyrs swift withdrawal left the state fragile, exposed, and distracted. That weakness, perceived or real, was all the opportunity needed.

At exactly 19:00, the Ministry of Magics wards and networks buckled under direct sabotage. The Array of Magical Oversight and Runestone Stabilization, the AMORS Network, which for centuries had kept magic suppressed, structured, and throttled into legality, collapsed. Centuries of equilibrium shattered in an instant.

The first signs were subtle. Lights dimmed without cause, electronic systems sputtered, and radio bands choked with static. By the second, more dramatic signs followed. The White Tree in the heart of Hyperion, long a silent monument, shone as though aflame, its bark white-gold, its leaves burning with radiant brilliance brighter than any daybreak. Its glow could be seen for miles, across states and provinces, by those who did not yet understand what was awakening around them.

[b]MAGIC RETURNED.[/b]

Runestones cracked, groaned, and bled light into the streets. The first to feel it were those who had never known power before. Ordinary men and women, children and elders, discovered their hands sparked, their voices bent reality, their dreams broke through into waking life. The weak became sorcerers in seconds. The learned practitioners, restrained their whole lives by AMORS, swelled with strength beyond comprehension, their senses and influence bursting past the mortal. And those who had always dwelt in magic, in secrecy, in patient shadow, felt the flood like air after drowning. They laughed. They screamed. They rose.

The chaos that followed was immediate. In every city came firestorms and unnatural plagues, rivers turned to silver, shadows moved without form, and monsters walked out of memory into the present. Rural hamlets saw beasts of bone and blood erupt from the soil. Graves disgorged their sleepers. Towers that had once been government offices now cast illusions as tall as mountains. And Hyperion, the old city, the heart of stone and myth, bloomed with the return of its ghosts and its long-slumbering horrors.

The Ministry of Magic, once bureaucratic and restrained, declared an [b]EMERGENCY STATE[/b]. But even their enforcers were overwhelmed. Their registries dissolved, their wards cracked, their agents scrambled. They struggled to decide if they were still regulators or now soldiers.

The military scrambled armor and infantry, but found their guns firing alongside bolts of conjured flame. Logistics broke down as convoys were struck by storms that never appeared on any forecast. The economy trembled as factories halted when spectral hands rewired the machines themselves.

And through it all, the White Tree glowed. Unblinking, unstoppable, unending.

Midnight approached, and with it, the final truth of this night. The Magnates, nine hundred in number, the industrial barons and financial dynasties that had long ruled the silent economy of the Empire, understood what it meant. They were prey. Their wealth, their fortresses, their contracts, meant nothing in a land where raw magic walked again. Their response was immediate. They gathered in a single, clandestine call, scattered across states but united in fear. And in that meeting was declared the [b]MIDNIGHT OPERATIONS[/b].

Twenty thousand dollars a month, per head, for any mercenary brave enough to answer the call. One million per Magnate rescued and returned alive. Bonuses for major kills, for saved assets, for destroyed threats. No deductions for dead mercenaries. Fines, however, for damaging government property or slaying the wrong targets. And most importantly, a warning, strange and terrible: death was magically impossible until November 1st, the date where the Ministry of Magic expected it for it to be able to restore AMORS. Between now and Hallows Eve, no person could truly die. They could fall, they could bleed, they could be broken and torn, but magic itself would drag them back until the Runestones returned. After Hallows Eve, however, all debts would be called. The wounds unfixed, the organs missing, the limbs lost, would collapse the body in an instant.

The message went out to every clandestine network, a communique; MIDNIGHT OPERATION [900,000,000$]/[20,000$/m]. Perhaps the most ambitious and expensive contract ever sent out.

In the streets of Hearth City, Kingsmount, and Avernus, word spread. The ports were safe, by virtue of half-working runestones still glowing weakly. These three became the last bastions, the entry points for all who dared to enter. From there, the road inland to Hyperion, to the 4th haven, and beyond, was choked with every nightmare magic could conjure. Meanwhile the Holy See cracked it's own runestones, ancient and most well kept of all, and beaconed itself into a holy mission.

The people armed themselves, as they always had. Shotguns and pistols cracked against demons of fire. Knives found the throats of specters. Homemade armor deflected claws and fangs. Vespurians did not cower, but they did not pretend either. They fought, and they endured. And in the ports, the mercenaries began to arrive, called by the gold and by the challenge. To cross a land where every death was deferred but every horror multiplied. To escort, to kill, to rescue, to profit.

[b]CASE EXECUTIVE: IMPERIO IMPERATOR[/b]

The proclamation did not happen with trumpet and fanfare. It happened with the dull, efficient thud of legislation hitting the emergency docket and a curt script read on every functioning channel, radio, and municipal loudspeaker. At 02:13, less than three hours after the AMORS array cracked and the White Tree flared white-gold in the sky, the Hyperian Constitution's emergency clause was invoked. The phrase chosen for the public dispatch was antique and blunt, an old formula dusted off for modern times, and it carried the force of law: [i]Case Executive: Imperio Imperator, effective forthwith.[/i]

The words were simple. The effect was absolute. Every ministerial desk that could still answer a phone answered one more command. The Head of State, Emperor Aurean I, was vested with supreme executive authority for the duration of the crisis. He became, by constitutional fiat and by the will of a frightened populace, the single locus of national command. Every branch of the armed forces, every arcane agency, and every emergency civil directorate fell, for the time being, under his immediate strategic control.

Inside the Imperial Palace, which still smouldered with the tense glow of a thousand emergency lamps, Aurean moved like a man who had never expected to have to do so. He had voted against this very moment hours before, in private, in the old ridiculous civic humility that had once marked his life. Now that the moment had come, there was no time for that bureaucratic modesty. He accepted the mandate with a voice that carried both fatigue and an inherited carefulness. In the chamber beside him, Old Reuben the phoenix stretched, ruffled the last of his singed feathers, and regarded the staff with an expression best translated as a grudging tolerance. Reuben would be moved as well, later, because optics could be sentimental only to an extent.

The first practical act of Imperio Imperator was simple and unromantic: secure the personhood of command. The Emperor's family, defined in statute as potential leverage and therefore a strategic risk, were evacuated under covert escort. Empress Eve, muscular and unflappable, refused every dramatization; she took charge of the logistics of their own relocation as if managing a military exercise. Within an hour she had ordered comms protocols, delegated household staff, and approved the relocation of their immediate kin to a subterranean complex known to the Palace as [u]THE DEEP VAULT[/u], code name HEMERA. HEMERA was an old civil-defense hold, retrofitted in peace time as a research and archive vault beneath the Imperial Heartland. Its corridors had hosted treaties and university archives; now its rooms would host the Emperor's nearest and indispensible household, shielded from both mundane and magical breach.

The movement of the family was staged as an ordinary caravan of state: lit vehicles, a procession of neutral vans, two unmarked armoured transports, and then the quiet, businesslike insertion into an elevator that descended beyond maps and municipal blueprints into the heart of the stone. Journalists were told the family was safe. The public watched the official picture of Aurean, a short statement, and then a silence heavy with relief.

But even as HEMERA received its new charges, the legal and administrative machinery ground up into action. The cabinet met in a reduced, secure session. The House of Appointed had been sent a formal communication; the House of Anointed received a more ceremonial missive. The proclamation emphasized necessary powers: control of mobilization, the authority to requisition private resources, temporary suspension of certain regulatory frameworks to expedite emergency works, direction of the AMORS repair teams, and the ability to impose national curfew and rationing. Judicial review was constrained by emergency scheduling, though emergency tribunals were activated to ensure at least the appearance of due process for matters that could not wait.

On the streets the effect was immediate. Military orders rolled down the chain. The Army, Navy, and Air Armoriesair being, in Hyperion, electric and magitech rather than fuelreceived coded directives. Ground forces were told to prioritize three things: protect the runestone repair nodes, secure the White Tree perimeter, and hold the great arteries that connected Hearth City, Kingsmount, Avernus, and Hyperion. The mechanized brigades that remained mobile formed rapid-response columns; engineers were paired with arcane units to act as mixed repair-and-defence teams. Unit communications switched from standard civil bands to encrypted channels the Ministry of Defence and the Imperial Staff had long kept for unlikely eventualities.

The Navyknown to many merely as the Emperor's sailorswas ordered to enforce maritime cordons around the port-havens, primarily to make sure that the midnight evacuation of magnates and other vulnerable persons did not turn into a chaotic mass exodus that would strip ports of resources. They were given strict rules of engagement: protect, intercept, deny. The sailors set up floating barriers and relay nodes, so that even failing runestones could be buoyed by arcane stabilizers for short periods. Nothing flew over Hyperion. Nothing that burned fuel crossed the tree's no-fly zone. All shipping that remained was electric or magitech powered and under direct naval oversight.

Perhaps the most delicate operation involved the Ministry of Magic. Their agents, bureaucrats, and arcane engineers were suddenly on the front line. Under Imperio Imperator's directive, the Ministry ceased to be a registry and became an operational lead. The AMORS repair teams were reconstituted into triage units. Each team was paired with a military escort, and each unit was given authority to do what civil procedure would normally forbid: appropriate private arcane caches, detain suspicious practitioners, and impose temporary wards with lethal enforcement if necessary. The Ministry's new orders were brutal in their blunt practicality. They were to secure the largest runestone farms first, set up temporary field wards, and triage recursive instability.

Arcane policing moved from deskwork to patrols. Agents who had once sat on endless registries now anchored wards, marched into ruins, and rewired damaged nodes. They had protocols for how to handle spontaneous magiceach action logged, each signatory recorded, each stabilization attempt guaranteed with the presence of at least two witnesses drawn from Ministry ranks and military engineering. In a country that had spent centuries debating arcane ethics, the debate ended in one simple note: order must be preserved to save the people.

Civil protections were issued next. Curfew regulations were drafted; municipal authorities were authorized to requisition buildings for shelter and food. The Treasury moved within the hour to restrict certain capital flows, not as punishment, but to prevent destabilizing capital flight; banks were ordered to open emergency credit lines for municipalities. Honoria Blackstone, the Minister of the Treasury and the voice of dry arithmetic in calmer times, was sent a classified brief and promptly ordered currency controls, temporary suspension of certain derivatives trading, and an emergency bond issuance to finance the AMORS repair effort. The Imperial Dollar's exchange bands were tightened; the state froze a minimal share of magnate assets, not to seize but to ensure they could not evaporate the critical capital the nation required. Those actions were unpopular in some circles, savage in others, but they were surgical, clearly aimed at keeping rail lines open and repair crews fed.

At ground level the regime of command revealed its less glamorous aspects. Public broadcasts enforced curfews and explained the need for centralized imperatives. Municipal civil-defense squads were mobilized to handle ration distribution. Emergency shelters were established in former municipal halls, museums, and converted warehouses. Local magistrates were given emergency jurisdiction to try looters and to adjudicate seizures. The courts, for all their tradition, made room for a thousand small decisions that would determine whether a city survived or fell into private anarchy.

On the arcane front, the Ministry of Magic compiled what they called the Stabilization Priority List. It was a ledger of nodes and runestones, ranked by their systemic importance. The White Tree, because of its unique macro-arcana, assumed a protective halo: legal orders declared the Tree an object of national patrimony, sacrosanct and under the direct custody of the Imperial Office. No private initiative could approach it without imperial sanction. It was an act both symbolic and practical. People needed a symbol of order; the Tree would be that symbol whether it consented to be or not.

Not every arm of the state cooperated at once. The bureaucracy had factions, as it always did: those who deferred to the civil service logic of continuity attempted to create working groups and checklists; the old imperialists wanted direct command lines and martial clarity; some regional governors feared the usurpation of autonomy. Imperio Imperator's proclamation included a final, administrative admonition: regional autonomy could not translate into fragmentation. Local leaders were told that their powers remained, but that national coherence was now directive. To make that stick, the Emperor deployed liaison officers to every provincial hall. They were not there to watch, the officers insisted; formally they were there to assist. Informally the officers ensured that military and arcane directives had teeth.

The civil service, in its own way, moved to make the executive functional. The Cabinet Secretary transformed the old daily orders into executable checklists. Specialized task forces formed: one for communications and propaganda control to prevent panic; one for logistics and food distribution; one for infrastructure recovery; one for hire and coordination of mercenary groups where appropriate; one exclusively for protecting critical cultural assets, including archives, museums, and the White Tree perimeter. Each task force took members from multiple ministries so that no single ministry would hoard power.

There were hard realities. The rule of Imperio Imperator justified extraordinary resource seizure. The state drafted requisition orders for heavy equipment and for private magitech reserves. The Magnates did not like it and murmured bitterly, but many signed compliance papers with the same hand that sent mercenaries out that night. The Midnight Operations were not outlawed; rather they were folded into an operative rubric. Mercenary contracts were reviewed, accredited, and parceled as subcontractors of the state rather than wholly private actors. This allowed the state to monitor the flow of arms, to ensure supply lines were not being siphoned to predatory elements, and to attach legal strings to payments.

Enforcement was visible on the streets. Armoured columns moved along the main arterials. Engineers in orange vests worked beside arcane technicians, their hands stained both oil and rune-etching chalk. Soldiers stood between frantic crowds and overloaded power nodes with orders to defend, but not to fire except on clear orders. The message was clear: force would be used, but prudently. The population responded with a mixture of terror, relief, and a peculiar Vespurian defiance. People boarded stores with sandwich boards that said simply, in the old, dry national humour, "We are busy saving the nation, stand by." In other districts, small militias formed under local watch committees, and the Imperial Staff negotiated with them for the pooling of arms and the local management of neighbourhood wardens.

The legal engines also adjusted. Emergency tribunals were convened for crimes related to sabotage and to arcane misuses. The Ministry of Justice set priority dockets for treason and runestone tampering. For the remainder of the night, judges in secure courthouses drafted fast-track warrants and attached them to combined military-arcane raids. These raids, when conducted, paired soldiers with Ministry wardens so that if an interdicted spell erupted the soldiers could contain the physical threat while the wardens attempted stabilization.

At the Palace, late into the night, the Emperor received briefings. He was briefed on the status of runestone nodes, the troop dispositions, the status of ports, the arcane triage, and the family safe in HEMERA. He signed requisitions that moved capital and material where engineers needed it. He authorized, under extraordinary measures, an order for several "Stabilization Cores"experimental magitech devices designed by a private consortium that had been working on limited arcane dampening. The cores were risky; they had never been deployed at scale. The Emperor judged that risk acceptable and authorized deployment to three critical nodes. The cores were escorted by military convoys and altar-wardens, rods of iron and ritual combined.

It was messy. It was legal, but not elegant. The proclamation of Imperio Imperator had concentrated authority at the apex where speed and clarity could matter, and the state began to operate like a single organism where it had previously been three. That had costs: local grievances, accusations of overreach, panic amongst the old liberal cadres, and a thousand little implacable bureaucratic irritations. But for every minor resentment, a soldier, a warden, an engineer, or a ration distribution team held a trembling hand and said, plainly, with the bluntness of practical men, that the alternative was worse.

[b]CASE ARCANE: ARCANUM ANTEBELLUM[/b]

The day after Imperio Imperator brought no calm. Instead, it brought collapse. The runestones failed to stabilize and the air of Vespurias grew denser with magic by the hour. What had been drained and weak for centuries was now flooding uncontrolled, thicker than anyone alive had ever experienced. The White Tree no longer looked like a national blessing. Its bark glowed white-gold, bright enough to leave marks in the eye, and its radiance only made the atmosphere worse.

The first signs were strange but not immediately violent. Lights appeared in empty fields, pockets of air bent in on themselves, and farm animals began to change shape into monstrous forms. Men and women who had never cast a spell suddenly tore apart walls or stalls with wild surges. Arguments ended with fire, panic, or blades drawn from thin air. Children woke in the night surrounded by shadows that refused to leave. None of it was coordinated. It was simply uncontrolled density, spilling into everyday life.

Then came the animals and monsters. Predators long believed to be myth ran loose from forests. In the south, wetlands gave rise to huge scaled beasts. Birds of prey with unnatural size were seen circling over towns, and reports came of wyverns climbing from caverns. The Ministry confirmed that the AMORS lattice had suppressed more than anyone had admitted, and now all of it was loose at once.

By the third night, the dead themselves were rising. Graves cracked open, bones marched from ossuaries, and rural cemeteries turned into battlefields. Villages fled as their ancestors dug out of the ground. Old soldiers in rusted armour dragged themselves from mounds, still carrying the rage of wars fought hundreds of years earlier. In places where whole armies had once died, the earth moved like a tide, giving rise to masses of the dead.

The Ministry of Magic could not cope. Their structure was built for paperwork, registries, and court hearings. Now they were at the front. Departments overlapped and tripped over each other. Law Enforcement tried to chase rogue sorcerers but ended up fighting hordes of monsters. The Department of Magical Creatures tried to contain outbreaks but was overrun in hours. The Department of Mysteries warned that planes themselves were thinning, that other realms were pressing into Vespurias. The crisis was not just domestic. It was dimensional.

Criminals and insurgents took advantage. Rituals that had been impossible to complete under the AMORS grid were suddenly easy. Wards collapsed. Forbidden rites succeeded. Basements turned into shrines. Whole blocks were taken over by men who declared themselves kings, priests, or gods. People were enslaved by sorcery. Demons, daemons, and other creatures were dragged into the material world by reckless hands. The surge made every dangerous temptation possible, and it happened too fast for anyone to stop all of it.

Reports became overwhelming. Fires consumed districts. Undead emptied villages. Magical storms blocked roads. Even breathing in the capital felt wrong, heavy, charged, unstable. The military warned the Ministry was no longer able to function under its old framework. Control was slipping hour by hour.

At 21:40, the second great proclamation was made. [i]Case Arcane: Arcanum Antebellum, effective forthwith.[/i]

The wording was blunt. The Ministry of Magic was given wartime powers equal to those of the armed forces. All rights to use magic were revoked. Every permit, every license, every old legal exemption, was invalid. Any offensive spell carried the death penalty. Any use of dark magic carried the death penalty. Any ritual of grade VII or higher carried the death penalty. Any creature or person using or causing level VII effects with intent would be executed.

The Ministry reorganized overnight. The Department of Mysteries was assigned intelligence and prediction of anomalies. The Department of Magical Creatures was treated as a combat corps to kill or drive out rampaging beasts. The Department of Magical Law Enforcement became execution squads with orders to kill rogue wizards before they could cause further harm. The Department of Magical Resources seized materials, reagents, and talismans for national use. The Department of Magical Archives closed its libraries and instead became planning hubs for containment. The Department of the Magical Treasury took control of enchanted assets and imposed full wartime rationing.

The first executions followed within hours. Rogue sorcerers who had summoned creatures into residential areas were taken into custody, condemned, and shot on broadcast. The message was immediate: the use of uncontrolled magic would not be tolerated under any circumstance.

Case Arcane turned the Ministry into something it had never been before. It was no longer a regulatory body. It became a war institution. Their agents patrolled streets with soldiers. They imposed wards on districts, they confiscated private stashes of artifacts, and they used lethal force when orders called for it. And anyone even using a wand to playfully summon something might end up looking at the end of a rifle barrel.

[b]THE FRACTURING[/b]

The weeks following Case Arcane saw no reprieve. The air remained heavy, the runestones remained fractured, and the crisis spread outward like cracks on glass. What had begun as scattered anomalies turned into the disintegration of social order across the Lands Between Havens, the wide stretch of provinces and townships that separated the four surviving safe zones: Hearth, Kingsmount, Avernus, and Hyperion.

By late March the landscape itself looked altered. Roads were unsafe, forests swarmed with warped creatures, and entire villages emptied overnight. Reports filtered in of monsters staking out their own territories, hunting humans not for food but for sport. Packs of direwolves roamed as organized predators. Drakes and wyverns claimed ruined farmsteads as nests. Some called them monster kings, beasts that rallied others of their kind.

But the human threat grew far sharper than the animal one. The collapse of the AMORS lattice was not only a disaster but an opportunity, and factions formed with ruthless speed.

Republican cells, long dormant, declared the imperial regime had failed. They targeted Ministry officials, bombing convoys and sabotaging runestone repair attempts. They armed themselves with whatever they could take from old stockpiles or loot from the chaos. Their message was simple: the Emperor had lost his mandate, the monarchy had no right to command.

Opposite them came the monarchist zealots, furious at what they saw as betrayal from within. They hunted Republicans, burned suspected sympathizers, and styled themselves as royal militias. Their loyalty to the Emperor was less useful than destructive, because they answered to no one but their own captains.

Then came the cults. Some worshipped the White Tree as a god reborn. Others declared the monsters spilling out of caverns as heralds of a new age. Necromancers, long buried in secrecy, walked openly with legions of dead at their back. Rural villages woke to find banners raised in the night, petty kings and self-proclaimed lords ruling by spell and sword.

Religious orders split. The Holy See called for purges of heresy and dispatched hunters into the Barrows. Witch hunters spread through the northern parishes, dragging suspected practitioners into pyres. Yet in the east, some sects embraced the chaos, insisting the surge was divine punishment and that all human law should fall.

Technological factions emerged as well. Techno-terrorists raided Ministry caches and tried to weaponize magitech against both monsters and men. Magi-terrorists, armed with spells once impossible, struck at government centers and declared themselves masters of a new magical democracy. Each faction contradicted the other. Each faction claimed legitimacy.

Adventuring guilds appeared as quickly as they had centuries ago, only now they resembled armed corporations more than bands of heroes. They offered bounties, contracts, and "insurance" to towns too small to defend themselves. Some fought monsters for coin. Others became bandits with paperwork.

Ordinary Vespurians did not sit idle. The culture of arms rose to the surface. Households kept rifles at the ready. Town militias formed checkpoints. Streets bristled with barricades. It was no longer unusual to see farmers carrying carbines while tending fields, or teachers leading classrooms with revolvers at their hip. Freedom meant survival, and survival meant firepower.

The Ministry of Magic and the military attempted to enforce order, but the country was tearing itself apart faster than directives could contain. Arcane patrols clashed with necromancers, soldiers exchanged fire with Republicans, civilians fought off both monsters and insurgents. No alliance held. Contradiction and avarice defined the landscape.

It was under this chaos that the third proclamation was read into law at 23:55 on March 30th. [i]Case Antiquity: Iudex Nihil, effective forthwith.[/i]

The declaration was dry, clinical, and absolute. The AMORS collapse was now acknowledged as total. The Empire had entered full state emergency.

Curfew was ordered from 07:00 to 19:00 nationwide. All executive authority was centralized. The mobilization of all military personnel was mandated. Allied and continental contacts were to be informed immediately. All air traffic ceased. The International Alliance was dispatched a pre-written communique admitting instability.

Legislation was suspended. Evacuation routes were marked. Operations Bastion, Resistance, and Armoury were placed into effect. Bastion meant fortified lines around the havens. Resistance meant coordination of irregular militias as auxiliaries. Armoury meant mass distribution of arms from state stockpiles.

Constitutional rights were preserved only in their most basic form. The Ministry of Magic and the Ministry of Defense were both elevated to over-cabinet federal authority. A War Council was reinstated, a body not convened in over a century. The capital was locked down under military executive command.

Most importantly, the capital was formally declared the epicenter of magical instability. The White Tree was closed off by decree. No one could approach it without direct sanction. Contingencies regarding the Tree were quietly put into preparation, the kind of plans spoken about only in whispers: containment, suppression, even destruction.

.

"Olha só, um garotinho rico vagando...imagino quanto nos pagariam se nos..."
Dois cangaceiros, vestidos em um poncho e bombacha, com um chapéu de aba larga e lenço branco no pescoço, eles apontaram duas facas para vossa alteza e disseram:
"Você aí, parado, pirralho."
Um deles sorriu com certa malícia em seus olhos, e então apontou para um cavalo marrom próximo.
"Só siga o que nós..."
Apesar do aviso, Leo pareceu irreverente quanto a isso, de fato, ignorou e passou no meio deles caminhando, como se eles nem existissem, ele sussurrou, inaudível:

Os dois olharam com incredulidade para o garoto, ofendidos obviamente, e então um colocou o pé na frente do caminho do príncipe, que tropeçou no chão, caindo de cara na grama, eles sorriram.
"Pare de falar baboseiras, seu pai certamente nos dará uma bela recompensa pelo seu resgate."
O outro cangaceiro então bateu no ombro do companheiro, com um tom meio de pressa:

O companheiro porém, não se importou, ao invés disso, ele levantou o príncipe pelo punho agarrando com um agarrão sujo, o príncipe parecia, assustado, mas tentava parecer forte mesmo assim.
"Bah, mas vamos lá Garrucha, só dessa vez."
O outro apenas cobre o rosto com a mão, fingindo hesitação, mas então solta uma risada:
"Gegegeheh, vamos lá então ensinar pra esse piá aí então."
Uéton respondeu com um sorriso, e então jogou o garoto contra a grama com um golpe de seu pulso contra seu rosto, com o príncipe sendo jogado contra a grama...
alguns minutos depois.
Enquanto alteza era erguido pela perna pelos cangaceiros, ele tentando lutar, em vão, se debatendo gritando;
"Eu...eu sou forte! Me larguem seus..."
[b]tack[/b].

[b]Tick[/b].

"Você é o pai do garoto? Se quiser-"

"vamos indo...garoto."
Ele tirou um palito do bolso de sua camisa e pôs no dente, parecendo relaxar, e então pegou o príncipe o colocando em suas costas, ainda inconsciente.
"Está tudo bem agora...vamos indo."
Algum tempo após, com o sol já se pondo e o céu laranja, e o príncipe recém acordando, ele apertou os braços ao redor do pescoço do capitão, com medo, e com um choro falou, com a voz soluçante:
"Maciel..."

"Você acordou..."
Mas o príncipe, não respondeu Maciel, ele afunda o rosto no ombro do capitão, com um choro abafado pelo tecido, ele agarrou o Alexandre com mais força.
"Eu só quero ser forte, eu quero..."
E repetiu isso várias e várias vezes, Maciel preferiu não responder, mas decidiu segurar sua mão suavemente, como um gesto de cuidado sutil, respondeu, não como se falasse ao filho do imperador, mas como uma criança frágil, que precisa de proteção:
"Eu sei..eu sei..."

2019, Pampas.
my lord, Prince Leo
Maciel glanced around. The fields stretched endlessly, it couldve been anywhere. The emperor had decided to take a vacation and left the state in the hands of the Prime Minister. While His Majesty was away, it was Maciels job to watch over the prince. But His Highness was a rather quick childeasy to get lost. The pampas were flat, giving a child free rein to run wherever he wanted, specifically, due to a urge to see nature out the sight of the honoured guard.

.
The prince:
The prince, a simple child who would turn ten later that year, wandered through the field, seemingly carefree, taking in the beauty of nature.
Look at that, a rich little boy wandering around I wonder how much we could get if we
Two cangaceiros appeared, wearing ponchos and baggy pants, wide-brimmed hats, and white scarves around their necks. They pointed knives at the boy.
You there! Stop, brat.
One of them grinned with a mischievous glint in his eyes and nodded toward a brown horse nearby.
Just follow our
Leo ignored them completely, strolling right between them as if they didnt exist. He whispered, just quietly enough to be unheard:
these Cangaceiros smell like booze
The two men looked at him in disbelief, clearly offended. One stepped into the boys path, making him trip and fall face-first into the grass. They smirked.
Stop babbling, your father will surely give us a nice reward for rescuing you.
The other tapped his companion impatiently on the shoulder.
Tsk, come on, Uéton.
But Uéton didnt care. Instead, he grabbed the prince by the wrist, a rough grip. The boy looked frightened but tried to stay brave.
Bah, come on, Garrucha, just this once.
The other covered his face, pretending hesitation, then laughed.
Gegegeheh, alright, lets teach this little brat a lesson.
Uéton smiled and swung the boy onto the grass with a quick twist of his wrist.
A few minutes later, the prince was dangling by his leg, struggling and shouting:
IIm strong! Let me go, you
[b]tack[/b].
A punch landed. Uéton looked at his partner.
Enough for today, Garrucha. Lets move.
Garrucha smiled and grabbed the prince by the neck. The boys face was swollen and streaked with tears. Just as he was about to strike again
[b]Tick[/b].
A toothpick struck Garruchas face precisely. It wasnt meant to hurt, only to distract. He instantly released the prince and turned to see Maciela tall man in simple but elegant clothes.
Are you the boys father? If you
One of the bandits tried to threaten him, but Maciel cut him off smoothly, his voice calm as if in casual conversation:
I only want the boy and you two to leave.
The two men laughed and raised their revolvers at Alexandre. He rolled his eyes.
I see..."
Leo lay on the grass, eyes watering, face bruised from the earlier attack. He murmured:
A Alexandre
Then he fainted. Maciel gestured briefly, and the air around him turned sharp like knives, slicing through the bandits weapons. They froze, eyes wide.
Witchcraft! Garrucha, get him! Ill cover the back!
But before they could react, Maciel shaped the sharp air into strong strands that bound the bandits and flung them aside.
He looked down at the heir, exhaling heavily.
Lets go kid."
He plucked a toothpick from his pocket, popped it in his mouth, and seemed to relax. Then he lifted the prince onto his back, still unconscious.
Everything is ok now my lord."
Some time later, with the sun setting and painting the sky orange, the prince awoke. Clinging to the captains neck, trembling, he sobbed:
Maciel
Alexandre didnt respond, just carried him safely, calm and steady, as if he were carrying his own child.
Youre awake..." 
he said in a simple tone.
But the prince didnt answer. He buried his face in the captains shoulder, muffling his sobs on the fabric, holding on tighter.
I just want to be strong, I want I want..."
He repeated it over and over. Maciel didnt reply but gently held his hand, a small gesture of care, speaking not as the emperors sons guardian but as to a fragile child who needed protection:
Yeah...yeah...I know.

Tessitores os quais não estão registrados no CNT são sempre dados e registrados como ameaças de alto nível nacional, já que não podem ser rastreados nem se tem informações plenas sobre eles.
Tessitores não registrados no CNT são estimados com cerca de 800, embora não seja totalmente conhecido.
Os não registrados são marcados em 3 categorias.
[b]Ameaça Alto nível:[/b] São poderosos e devem ser limitados, o combate direto contra um seria, insensato, é preferível ter cautela e estar um passo a frente deles para que seus planos não se concretizem, pois caso aconteçam, a ordem nacional pode ser afetada. 
[b]Ameaça intermediária:[/b] Não registrados de nível intermediário podem ser combatidos e caçados, mas o EIHE prefere os vigiar, e manter o olho sobre eles semelhante aos de Alto Nível.
[b]Baixa ameaça:[/b] Sem ameaça significativa nos olhos do EIHE, podem e sempre que possível, serem rastreados e capturados, alguns são apenas Tessitores os quais são de baixa ameaça são, na verdade , os que vivem em áreas remotas sem conhecimento do registro, portanto após serem localizados um agente é designado para o levar até o registro,  o foco do EIHE para os não registrados é de capturar e tornar seus agentes, não matar, isso é apenas em último caso.
A ordem geral do EIHE para lidar com os não registrados é, captura.
A forma a qual são classificados é de acordo com a ameaça que apresentam ao império, no caso de , por exemplo um Tessitor declarar guerra diretamente ao império é uma forma de Ameaça de Alto nível independente do poder.
[b] Níveis dos Tessitores no CNT:[/b]
[b]Classe 0:[/b] também conhecida como Classe Especial, o poder deles é algo imensurável e potencial de destruição é algo imenso, até hoje no CNT só houveram 3 casos registrados de Classes 0, um dos quais é o capitão da Guarda de Honra, Alexandre Maciel, eles são considerados forças da natureza cujo potencial é uma ameaça a toda nação.
[b]Classe 1:[/b] poderosos mas ainda abaixo dos de classe 0, são Tessitores poderosos, são os aptos para liderar e treinarem outros Tessitores. São o ápice que um Tessitor pode esperar chegar, são confiados a ensinarem os Tessitores em uma das escolas possíveis, o EIHE os confia a missões de alto risco pois sabe que pode contar com eles perfeitamente pelo seu alto poder, é o máximo que um Tessitor pode esperar chegar já que a Classe 0 é um caso totalmente diferente e especial, existem um total de 10 agentes da classe 1 atualmente, responsáveis pelo ensino de uma das três escolas.
É de se esperar que cada classe 1 tenha ao menos algum domínio sobre mais de uma das escolas.
Sempre devem acompanhar seus alunos em missões de alto risco.
[b]Classe 2:[/b] são excepcionalmente habilidosos e acima da média, já foram bem treinados pelos classe 1 ao nível de poderem ser levados a missões sozinhos quando não forem de alto risco. Em alguns casos podem haver até servirem de auxiliares dos Classe 1 em ensinar classes abaixo, existem um total de 38 agentes classe 2 atualmente.
[b]Classe 3:[/b] a média, onde a maioria dos agentes estão, existem um total 156 de classes 3, são os "agentes de campo" os quais realizam as missões e treinamento sob a supervisão de um Classe 1 ou em alguns casos Classe 2 em missões de menor risco. A maioria dos Tessitores qualificados  estão nesta classe, geralmente lidam com ameaças de baixo nível acompanhados por classes 2.
[b]Classe 4:[/b] São Tessitores qualificados notavelmente fracos e inexperientes, por algum motivo, mesmo treinados não conseguem apresentar capacidade de "subirem" de classe, essa classe é dada apenas após uma profunda análise, existem cerca de 77 classes 4 registrados, geralmente são acompanhados por classes 2 para suas missões, é só são enviados para missões solo se forem de baixo ou baixo-médio risco.
[b]Classe 5[/b]: aprendizes, muitos crianças ou jovens adolescentes, ainda em fase de treinamento, são muitos, cerca de 402, são treinados pelos Classe 1 e 2, não são enviados em missões para treinarem e seus poderes são limitados apenas ao uso nos centros de treinamento.

O processo de treinamento é algo confidencial, limitado aos centros do EIHE, um juramento é feito pelos Tessitores de jamais revelarem aos de fora.

Tessitores who are not registered in the CNT are always classified and recorded as high-level national threats, since they cannot be tracked and there is no complete information about them.
Unregistered Tessitores are estimated to number around 800, although the exact figure is unknown.
The unregistered are categorized into three groups.

[b]High-level Threat:[/b] They are powerful and must be contained. Engaging one directly would be unwise; it is preferable to act with caution and stay one step ahead of them so their plans do not come to fruition, as that could endanger national order.

[b]Intermediate Threat:[/b] Unregistered individuals of intermediate level can be fought and hunted, but the EIHE prefers to keep them under surveillance, monitoring them similarly to those of High Level.

[b]Low Threat:[/b] Considered insignificant by the EIHE, they canand whenever possible, shouldbe tracked and captured. Some Low Threat Tessitores are, in fact, individuals living in remote areas unaware of the registration system; therefore, once located, an agent is assigned to escort them for registration. The EIHEs main objective regarding the unregistered is to capture and recruit them, not kill themthat is only a last resort.

The general EIHE order for dealing with the unregistered is: capture.
Classification depends on the threat they pose to the empire. For example, if a Tessitor were to declare war directly on the empire, that would automatically make them a High-level Threat regardless of their power.

[b]Levels of the Tessitores in the CNT:[/b]

[b]Class 0:[/b] Also known as Special Class. Their power is immeasurable, and their destructive potential immense. To this day, there have only been three recorded Class 0 cases in the CNT, one of them being the Captain of the Honor Guard, Alexandre Maciel. They are considered forces of nature, whose potential poses a threat to the entire nation.

[b]Class 1:[/b] Powerful, but still below Class 0. These are highly skilled Tessitores, capable of leading and training others. They represent the pinnacle a Tessitor can aspire to reach. They are entrusted with teaching Tessitores in one of the schools, and the EIHE assigns them to high-risk missions, knowing it can rely on their great power. This is the highest level a Tessitor can normally achieve, since Class 0 is an entirely separate and special case. There are currently 10 Class 1 agents, each responsible for teaching at one of the three schools.
Each Class 1 is expected to have mastery over more than one school.
They must always accompany their students on high-risk missions.

[b]Class 2:[/b] Exceptionally skilled and above average, they have been well-trained by Class 1 agents to the point of being able to undertake solo missions when not high-risk. In some cases, they may even assist Class 1 agents in teaching lower classes. There are currently 38 Class 2 agents.

[b]Class 3:[/b] The average level, where most agents fall. There are 156 Class 3 agents in total. They are the "field agents" who carry out missions and training under the supervision of a Class 1 or, in some cases, a Class 2 agent for lower-risk missions. Most qualified Tessitores belong to this class, and they usually handle low-level threats accompanied by Class 2 agents.

[b]Class 4:[/b] These are qualified Tessitores who are notably weak or inexperienced. For some reason, even with training, they fail to demonstrate the capability to advance in class. This classification is assigned only after deep evaluation. There are about 77 Class 4 agents registered. They are usually accompanied by Class 2 agents on missions and are only sent alone on low or low-medium risk missions.

[b]Class 5:[/b] Apprentices, mostly children or young teenagers still in the training phase. They are numerous, around 402 in total. They are trained by Class 1 and Class 2 agents and are not sent on missions. Their powers are restricted to use within training centers.

The training process is confidential, limited to EIHE centers. Tessitores take an oath never to reveal it to outsiders.
